items.text: A 175-year-old hurricane record has been broken as experts reveal surprising storm news for 2027
items.article: Hurricane experts have never seen anything like what is happening in the Atlantic Ocean this year, and it is having a major impact on Americans in storm-prone areas. By CHRIS MELORE, US DEPUTY SCIENCE EDITOR Published: 16:21, 17 September 2026 | Updated: 18:12, 17 September 2026 The Atlantic hurricane season has just reached a shocking milestone and weather experts say Americans have not seen anything like this in at least 175 years. As of Thursday, there has not been a single hurricane in the Atlantic Ocean in 2026. That is the latest into a year there have been no tropical cyclones to reach hurricane strength - meaning its winds reached 74mph. Scientists have been keeping records of hurricanes since 1851. Although this data is sometimes incomplete, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has said the last time the first hurricane of the season formed this late was in 1941. The National Hurricane Center revealed on Thursday that there is currently only one disturbance in the Atlantic that has any chance of turning into a tropical cyclone , and that weather system only has a 40 percent chance of forming by next week.

The 'help wanted' ad was posted by Amentum, a government contractor which provides technical and support work for the US military, who is searching for a first officer and co-pilot based in Las Vegas . items.article: John Studzinski answers our burning questions Published: 11:09, 25 September 2026 | Updated: 11:33, 25 September 2026 Risk Society by the German sociologist Ulrich Beck. Rather than drawing glib conclusions, he asks probing questions. Beck’s premise is that the greater sophistication of society has brought greater anxiety with it. The threats we face today –from artificial intelligence , to cyber attacks and financial crises – are the product of our own, unchecked ingenuity. What I admire most is Beck’s refusal to promise certainty. In an age when politicians, pundits and social media influencers all claim to have the answers to our problems, he offers something more valuable, and that’s humility. Only if we acknowledge that almost everything in life is uncertain can we start to gain wisdom. the Bible and Tolstoy’s War And Peace. Nothing matches the Bible for a profound understanding of human nature – love, betrayal, ambition, hope, forgiveness, suffering, redemption. At 20, you read it looking for answers; at 40, for guidance; later in life, for wisdom and perspective. It’s a lifelong conversation. As for War And Peace, every time I return to it I discover something new. Tolstoy embraces humanity in all its scope and detail, complexity and imperfection.

items.article: A new snow map suggests that most of the US may be robbed of seeing a white Christmas in 2026 due to a record-breaking weather phenomenon. By CHRIS MELORE, US DEPUTY SCIENCE EDITOR Published: 16:00, 13 September 2026 | Updated: 16:00, 13 September 2026 A new forecasting map has revealed how more than half the US could be robbed of a white Christmas this year due to the global weather changes bought on by El Niño. The weather phenomenon, which increases ocean temperatures in the Pacific and flips global weather patterns, is now predicted to lower the chances of there being snow in late December across the Northeast, Midwest and Northern Plains. Overall, 26 states have been given a 'lower-than-average chance' of seeing a white Christmas, meaning at least one inch of snow on the ground by Christmas morning. This includes traditionally wintry states such as New York, New Jersey , Pennsylvania , Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota , Wisconsin , the Dakotas and the entire New England area.

items.text: Putting Thailand at the center of global conversations
items.article: As Bangkok prepares to host the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group, Thailand is building on its track record as a destination for major international business events. As Bangkok prepares to host the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group, Thailand is building on its track record as a destination for major international business events. Supported by established infrastructure, government and industry cooperation, and a nationwide MICE network, the country is attracting gatherings that bring together global industries, decision-makers, and ideas. From October 12 to 18, 2026, Bangkok will host the 2026 IMF–World Bank Group Annual Meetings, bringing together more than 15,000 global financial leaders and senior government officials from 191 countries—the culmination of years of collaboration across government and the country’s MICE or business events industry. As Thailand’s national bidder for international business events, the Thailand Convention and Exhibition Bureau (TCEB) worked with the Ministry of Finance over several years to support the successful bid. A government agency under the supervision of the Prime Minister, TCEB works with public- and private-sector partners to attract large-scale business events and build business connections.
